question: For domestic tariff, one unit of electrical energy consumption is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**kilowatt-hour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• One unit of electrical energy consumption is equivalent to one kilowatt-hour (kWh).
 
• 1 kilowatt-hour is equal to 3.6 million joules (3.6 MJ).
 
• It is a common unit of energy used by utility companies to measure electricity consumption.
 
• This unit is often seen on electricity bills indicating the amount of energy consumed.
 
• 1 kilowatt-hour represents the energy consumption of a device with a power of 1 kilowatt running for 1 hour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule (J)**

 
 
• It is the SI unit of energy.
 
• One joule is defined as the energy transferred when applying a force of one newton over a distance of one meter.
 
• 1 kilowatt-hour is equal to 3.6 million joules (3.6 MJ).
 
 
 
• **Watt (W)**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of power.
 
• One watt is equal to one joule per second.
 
• It measures the rate at which energy is used or produced.
 
 
 
• **Power and Energy Relationship**
 
 
• Power is the rate at which energy is consumed or produced.
 
• Energy consumption over time can be calculated by multiplying power by the duration of time.
 
• For example, a 100-watt bulb running for 10 hours consumes 1 kilowatt-hour of energy.
 
 
 
• **Electricity Billing**
 
 
• Electricity bills are typically calculated based on the number of kilowatt-hours consumed.
 
• Utility companies charge a specific rate per kilowatt-hour of energy used.
 
• Energy consumption is monitored through electricity meters installed at consumer premises.
